events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven by boat.** I'd expect this week's boat fishing there to be about **3 of 4**. Muskegon is the backup at about 2.
- Fish about 90-120 ft of water, with lines running 50-100 ft down.
- Use glow plugs and glow spoons, mainly at first light and in low light.
- Ratings for the other ports, my expectations for boats this week: **Muskegon 2**, **South Haven 2**, **St. Joseph 1-2** (its only recent boat report is three weeks old and unrated).
- Check the wind forecast before you go. I have no wind data for this week, and the water is only about 70 F.

## Why

- Grand Haven's most recent boat reports were the best of the four ports: quality 2 on Aug 19 and quality 3 on Aug 12 (Grand Haven, 2026-08-19; Grand Haven, 2026-08-12).
- Glow plugs and glow spoons were the lures that worked in the recent Muskegon and Grand Haven boat reports (Muskegon, 2026-08-19; Grand Haven, 2026-08-19).
- I'd expect fish to stay in the 50-100 ft band because that is where recent boats found them, and cold water sits deeper as the lake warms (Grand Haven, 2026-08-19).
- Muskegon's last boat report with a rating was average, and its Aug 12 report was slow when water was warm (Muskegon, 2026-08-19; Muskegon, 2026-08-12).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is Aug 26, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, Aug 19, boat: "Boat anglers found decent numbers of salmon 55 to 100 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water… Glow plugs worked well in low-light conditions." Quality 2.
- Grand Haven, Aug 12, boat: "Salmon were caught 50 to 90 feet down in 85 to 150 feet of water… Blue and green spoons worked well, along with a white flasher-fly combo." Quality 3.
- Muskegon, Aug 26, boat: "Boat anglers caught salmon from the breakwalls out to 80 feet of water… Glow plugs and glow spoons worked best." Not rated.
- Muskegon, Aug 19, boat: best action "50 to 100 feet down in 90 to 170 feet of water." Quality 2 for Chinook.
- Muskegon, Aug 12, boat: "Anglers targeting salmon were unsuccessful due to warm water." Quality 0.
- South Haven, Aug 12, boat: "A fair number of salmon were reported 45 to 90 feet down in 100 to 130 feet of water. Green or blue glow spoons worked well." Quality 2.
- St. Joseph, Aug 12, boat: "Salmon along with a few steelhead 55 to 80 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water… White flasher-fly combinations and glow spoons." Not rated.
- No South Haven or St. Joseph reports after Aug 12 were in the database.

**Past seasons (history, similar water temperature around Sept 1)**
- Boats did well in similar water in some past years: Grand Haven, 2025-08-20 (quality 3, 50-100 ft down); South Haven, 2024-08-28 (quality 3, beyond 110 ft); South Haven, 2022-09-07 (quality 3).
- Warm, flat weeks were often slow: Muskegon, 2024-08-28 (quality 0); St. Joseph, 2024-09-04 (quality 0, "best water well beyond 100 feet").
- Piers were slow in most of these weeks, so boats are the better bet here.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode and gave the week before Sept 1, not live readings. Buoy surface water that week was: St. Joseph 74 F (down 2 F), South Haven 71 F (flat), Grand Haven and Muskegon 70 F (up 2 F).
- The Aug 26 Grand Haven report noted a sharp 4 F drop, which the DNR linked to possible upwelling (Grand Haven, 2026-08-26). Water has since warmed again.
- The wind forecast was not available.

## Caveats

- The newest report is Aug 26, so these ratings come from reports up to six days old and from recent weeks. Fall conditions change fast.
- The "current" temperatures came from a backtest summary, not live data. Muskegon and Grand Haven share the same buoy in that summary.
- The 3-of-4 rating for Grand Haven is my expectation from two recent boat reports. It is not a forecast from the DNR.
- The St. Joseph rating is weakly supported. Its only recent boat report was not rated and is three weeks old.

- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Aug 19: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/425abbc
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven and St. Joseph, Aug 12: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/424a154
